definition: See Explainable AI — the broader property and set of techniques for making AI system behavior understandable to humans.
details: Explainability is closely related to but distinct from interpretability; explainability often emphasizes providing human-understandable justifications for outputs, while interpretability emphasizes understanding the model's internal mechanisms.

explainer.lead: Explainability is the ability to give people an understandable account of what an AI system did or why it produced an output. It matters because a useful answer alone may not be enough when someone needs to review, question, or trust a decision.

tiers.eli5: Imagine a robot sorts your drawings into piles but never tells you why. Explainability is like the robot saying, “I put this one here because it shows a dog,” so you can understand its choice and spot a possible mistake.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers apply explainability when users or reviewers need human-readable reasons for an AI output, such as the factors associated with a decision. A key pitfall is treating a fluent justification as evidence that it faithfully describes the system’s behavior or that the output is correct. Work on internal model mechanisms belongs more specifically to interpretability.
tiers.paperLevel: For a system f with input x and output y = f(x), explainability concerns producing a human-understandable account of y or of the system’s broader behavior. It is distinct from interpretability, which emphasizes understanding internal mechanisms. An explanation’s clarity alone does not establish that the output is correct or that the account faithfully describes the computation.

explainer.example: An AI system rejects a loan application. An explainable response might say that the decision was associated with a low stated income and several missed payments, giving the applicant concrete reasons to review instead of only a rejection.

usedIn.name: Decision support
usedIn.detail: Giving reviewers reasons they can consider alongside an AI system’s recommendation.

usedIn.name: User-facing AI
usedIn.detail: Helping people understand why they received a particular output.

usedIn.name: AI safety and governance
usedIn.detail: Supporting human scrutiny of system behavior and individual decisions.

explainer.intuition: An AI output becomes explainable when a person can receive a meaningful account of the behavior behind it, rather than only seeing the final result. The emphasis is on human understanding, not necessarily on exposing every internal calculation.
howItWorks: Start with an input and the AI system’s output.
Identify information relevant to accounting for that output or behavior.
Present that account in language the intended person can understand.
Use the explanation to review the result and identify possible problems.
explainer.whyItMatters: Explainability helps people question outputs, communicate about system behavior, and decide whether further review is needed. It also gives engineers and reviewers a human-readable starting point for examining possible failures.
misconceptions: Explainability and interpretability are identical: the former often concerns output justifications, while the latter emphasizes internal mechanisms.
A convincing explanation proves that the AI output is correct.
Every explanation must reveal all of a model’s internal computations.
